cannot.name: Public HTTPS address / TLS
cannot.plain: The product has no https:// web address and no certificate.
cannot.why: The deployer hands out only `http://{server_ip}:{port}`; a product's compose has no TLS proxy.
cannot.workaround: Use the Telegram bot as the product's interface; it needs no address. Programs that accept plain http can call the backend at http://<server IP>:<port>.

cannot.name: Custom domain
cannot.plain: The product cannot be put on its own domain name, such as mybot.example.com.
cannot.why: Nothing allocates, points or verifies a domain for a product; its address is the server IP.
cannot.workaround: Use the Telegram bot, or the backend at http://<server IP>:<port>.

cannot.name: Inbound webhooks from external services
cannot.plain: Other services (payments, GitHub, forms, Telegram webhook mode) cannot push events to the product.
cannot.why: Providers require an https URL, and the product only has plain http on an IP and port that can change when it moves server; the resolver derives no `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`.
cannot.workaround: Poll the provider's API on a timer; the Telegram bot already works this way (long polling).

cannot.name: The product knowing its own public URL
cannot.plain: The product cannot build links to itself, such as a link a user opens in a browser.
cannot.why: The resolver computes no `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` or similar derived key; a required unknown derived key fails the deploy with `Unknown computed secret` (story-92b433c8).
cannot.workaround: Send the information inside the Telegram chat rather than as a link to the product.

cannot.name: OAuth web sign-in redirects
cannot.plain: The product cannot use "Sign in with Google" style web redirects to get access to a user's account.
cannot.why: An OAuth web redirect needs an https redirect URL on a stable domain, which a product does not have.
cannot.workaround: A Google service account the user shares their calendar or sheet with; a device-code or desktop flow where the provider supports one; or a personal API token the user pastes, stored as a user secret.

cannot.name: Telegram Mini App or web pages inside Telegram
cannot.plain: The bot cannot open its own web app inside Telegram.
cannot.why: A Telegram Mini App needs an https URL, which a product does not have.
cannot.workaround: Build the interaction as chat messages with buttons.

cannot.name: Sending email by itself
cannot.plain: The product has no mail server of its own to send email.
cannot.why: The kit has no mail module and the platform provisions no mail server or SMTP relay.
cannot.workaround: Send through a third-party email API with a key the user provides (an outbound call), or send the message through the Telegram bot.

cannot.name: File storage beyond the database
cannot.plain: Uploaded files are not kept on disk; only data in the database survives an update.
cannot.why: The only persistent volume is Postgres's `db_data`; the backend and bot containers have no volume and are replaced on every deploy, and the kit has no object-storage module.
cannot.workaround: Keep small files in the database; keep Telegram files by their Telegram file id; or use an external storage service with credentials the user provides.

cannot.name: A schedule run by the platform
cannot.plain: The platform does not start the product's jobs on a clock.
cannot.why: The kit's jobs core schedules nothing, and the platform fires a product's jobs only during QA.
cannot.workaround: Run a timer loop inside the product's bot or backend process (see "Work on a timer").

cannot.name: A separate website or web app module
cannot.plain: The product cannot have its own website front end as a separate part.
cannot.why: A product may request only the `backend` and `tg_bot` modules; `frontend` and `notifications` remain only for old records, and only the backend's port is published.
cannot.workaround: Use the Telegram bot as the interface, or simple pages served by the backend at http://<server IP>:<port>.

cannot.name: Reaching the database from outside
cannot.plain: Nobody outside the server can connect to the product's database or Redis directly.
cannot.why: Postgres and Redis get host ports allocated, but production compose publishes only the backend's port and the firewall opens only that one.
cannot.workaround: Expose what is needed through backend endpoints.
